body.statement:
Let \(\delta_n=2^{-p_n-1}\), let \(\mathcal B_n\) be the coordinate box of radius \(\delta_n\) about \((\widetilde X,\widetilde R,\widetilde C)\) on \(\kappa_n=0\), and suppose the public controls are exact dyadic inputs.  Put
\[
\mathcal H_n=n+T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\alpha^{-1}+p_n+q_n+1.
\]
There are finite constants \(K_\star,k_\star\), depending only on \(c,C_0,B,\sigma,r_0\), such that for all sufficiently large \(n>r_0\), if every coordinate of \(\mathcal B_n\) is at most \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1\) in absolute value, then
\[
0\le\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}
\le K_\star\mathcal H_n^{k_\star}.
\]
If in addition every donor matrix \(X'\in\mathcal B_n\) satisfies
\[
s_r(X')\ge3cn/4,\qquad s_{r+1}(X')\le cn/4,
\qquad s_1(X')\le3C_0n/2,
\]
then
\[
\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}
\le K_\star\mathcal H_n^{k_\star}
\bigl(2^{-p_n}+2^{1-q_n}\bigr).
\]
Every nonnegative radius recorded as a summand of either \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\) or \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}\) obeys the corresponding upper bound.
body.proof_tex:
On \(\kappa_n=0\), every point of \(\mathcal B_n\) has coordinate magnitude at most \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1\).  The gate implies, at every feasible on-gate point,
\[
\|X_r^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\frac{2}{cn},
\qquad
\|Z_{p,n}\|_2,\|Z_{q,n}\|_2
\le\frac{\sqrt n(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1)}{\sigma}.
\tag{1}
\]
Consequently the center, analytic half-width, donor allowance, and every feasible on-gate endpoint are bounded by a fixed polynomial in \(\mathcal H_n=n+T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\alpha^{-1}+p_n+q_n+1\).  The off-gate interval has fixed radius \(M_0=B^2/c\).  Hence the hull of all feasible branches is contained in \([-K\mathcal H_n^k,K\mathcal H_n^k]\).  The certified handle may stop at that hull, so
\[
0\le\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}
\le K\mathcal H_n^k.
\tag{2}
\]
Exact-dyadic public controls have input radius zero.

Now assume the three stable spectral inequalities.  With \(\tau=(cn/2)^2\), the retained and discarded squared singular values are separated from \(\tau\) by at least
\[
\min\left\{(3cn/4)^2-(cn/2)^2,
(cn/2)^2-(cn/4)^2\right\}
=\frac{3c^2n^2}{16}.
\tag{3}
\]
The corrected \(\textup{lem:certified-error-recurrence}\) applies.  Its Newton--Schulz residual construction, explicit matrix-sign tail, noncommutative recurrence, and scalar propagation prove that the sharp branch is certified whenever the precision inequality in that lemma holds, and then
\[
\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}
\le K\mathcal H_n^k(2^{-p_n}+2^{1-q_n}).
\tag{4}
\]
If that precision inequality fails, it says \(1\le K\mathcal H_n^d(2^{-p_n}+2^{1-q_n})\).  Multiplying (2) by this inequality and increasing the exponent gives (4) again.  Thus (4) holds without silently assuming adequate precision.  Every recorded summand is nonnegative and at most the displayed sum, which proves the final assertion.
body.justification: The stable-box lemma converts the recurrence into a uniform observable padding bound and retains a valid coarse-hull case at inadequate precision.
body.gap: The bound includes input and working precision in its polynomial majorant and applies summand by summand.
body.consumer: The statistical transfer can integrate numerical padding rather than relying on a high-probability backward-error slogan.
